messages:
alex: Heads-up: saw 6 spot GPU node termination notices in us-west-2 over the last hour, all training jobs got killed mid-checkpoint. Need a low-latency handoff plan so long-running pods survive or at least resume without wasted GPU-hours.

oncall-bot: NodeTermination signal received: instance i-0abc123def in asg-spot-gpu-usw2a. lifecycle-hook: TERMINATING -> SQS message posted.

sana: Are we sure node-termination-handler is running everywhere? That should trigger cordon + annotate early. If notices are <120s it's still tight. Idea: ASG lifecycle hook -> SQS -> node agent extends termination deadline and applies a "soft-evict" taint so pods can react.

mike: We're running kube-node-termination-handler but it's not fast enough for short notices. Proposal: "soft-evict" flow where we add taint spot/preempt=soft:NoExecute and a lightweight sidecar checkpoints state in <30s, then we let CA scale up ondemand fallback.

jin: CA tweaks we should consider: increase --max-node-provision-time to 10m, set --scale-down-unneeded-time higher to avoid killing nodes during rebalancing, enable --balance-similar-node-groups. Also separate node groups by priority class to avoid evicting critical infra.

katie: Cost check: if we add 10% ondemand fallback capacity, what's the monthly delta? Also, what's the cost of wasted GPU-hours from restarts? Need a quick tradeoff table.

mike: Back-of-envelope: for our baseline fleet, 10% ondemand replaces ~200 GPU-hours/week -> ~ $800/wk delta at current pricing. But restart waste could easily exceed that if long jobs re-run. I'll run precise numbers.

sana: Implementation sketch: ASG lifecycle hook adds a 300s pre-terminate window. Node agent on hook: cordon -> apply taint spot/preempt=soft:NoExecute -> annotate node with preempt=grace:300. Pods with toleration+sidecar checkpoint quickly. For legacy pods without support, CA will trigger ondemand pool scale-up with label fallback=ondemand and we gracefully migrate by creationCost.

alex: That sounds reasonable. We should avoid full drains to minimize eviction churn. Can we also use PodDisruptionBudgets + priorityClasses for infra-critical pods?

jin: Yes — PDBs for critical services, priorityClass to pin important jobs to reserved node groups (ondemand). Also use topology spread constraints to avoid all checkpoints hitting the same storage gateway.

katie: +1. Add metric: preempt-rate, avg-restart-time, wasted-GPU-hours, ondemand-cost-delta. We'll need a dashboard to evaluate the canary.

mike: I'll put together a runbook + Terraform for a small ondemand node group (label=canary-preempt-2026) and lifecycle hook wiring. Canary plan: enable in us-west-2a for non-critical training queue only.

sana: I'll prototype node-agent changes and a Helm chart for the soft-evict taint logic. Sidecar example for checkpointing (very rough):
```
- name: checkpoint-sidecar
  image: registry/redwood/checkpoint:latest
  args: ["--flush-to", "s3://redwood-checkpoints"]
```

alex: Action items: mike -> runbook + TF + cost PR, jin -> CA flags + PDBs, sana -> node-agent + Helm, katie -> cost dashboard + alert thresholds. Target: canary in 72h. Ping here when changes are in a branch. :thumbsup:
